 Re : IA No. CRAN 2 of 2026  1.
In spite of service nobody appears for the victim girl/defacto complainant.
2. The petitioner was convicted under Section 376(2)(f) of the IPC and sentenced to suffer rigorous imprisonment for 12 years.
He says that he is in custody, post conviction, for about seven months.
He prays for suspension of sentence.
3. The petitioner says that there are several loopholes in the judgment and order impugned in this appeal.
The evidence on record does not support the prosecution case.
The false complaint was lodged because the petitioner was a creditor of the family of the victim.
4. Learned State Advocate opposes the prayer.
She says that the evidence of the victim girl is sufficient to sustain the conviction.

sentences.text: We have seen the materials on record and the evidence recorded before the learned Trial Judge.
The victim being PW 1 clearly narrates how the petitioner violated her in the petitioner's shop room.
The evidence of the first examining doctor being PW 9, prima facie, supports the prosecution case.
We also see that no suggestion was given on behalf of the defence that the petitioner was a creditor of the victim's family.
6. CRAN 2 of 2026 stands dismissed.

7. All observations made in this order are prima facie and only for the purpose of disposing of this application for suspension of sentence and the same shall have no bearing on the hearing of the appeal.
8. Section is directed to supply urgent photostat certified copies of this order to the parties, if applied for, upon compliance of all necessary formalities.
IN Re: CRA (DB) 447 of 2025:
9. The department is directed to ensure that paper book in connection with this appeal is ready by the end of May, 2026.

10. Place the appeal in the combined Monthly List of June, 2026 amongst the first 15 items.
( Apurba Sinha Ray, J. ) ( Arijit Banerjee, J. )
